content.title: Post-PCI care and risk assessment (selected excerpt)

early_discharge_criteria.summary: Selected low-risk patients may be suitable for early (including same-day) discharge after successful PCI/PPCI.
examples_of_criteria: Haemodynamically stable, not requiring vasoactive or mechanical support
early_discharge_criteria.notes: A consensus document and flow chart support decision-making on post-procedural length of stay.

content.transfer_practice: Early (same-day) transfer to a local hospital after successful PPCI is routine in selected patients under adequate monitoring and supervision, if no signs of ongoing ischaemia or arrhythmias and haemodynamically stable.
content.risk_assessment_overview: Early and late risk stratification soon after presentation is useful to aid decision-making in patients with ACS.

clinical_risk_assessment.recommendation: All patients with ACS (particularly STEMI) should have early assessment of short-term risk.
parameters_to_evaluate: Clinical markers of high risk (older age, tachycardia, hypotension, Killip class > I, anterior MI, previous MI, elevated initial serum creatinine, history of HF, peripheral arterial disease, anaemia)
clinical_risk_assessment.risk_scores: Several risk scores exist; the GRACE risk score offers the best discriminative performance and is recommended for risk assessment.

imaging_risk_assessment.key_point: LV dysfunction is a key prognostic factor for patients with ACS.
recommendations: Determine LVEF before hospital discharge in all patients with ACS.
Routine echocardiography after PPCI to assess resting LV, RV, and valvular function and to exclude early mechanical complications and LV thrombus.
If echocardiography is suboptimal or inconclusive, CMR may be a valuable alternative.

content.revascularization_considerations: In patients presenting days after an acute ACS event with completed MI, documented ischaemia or proven viability in a large myocardial territory may guide planned revascularization of an occluded IRA.
